UNIT.substrand: Sub-Strand2.5: Area of a Part of a Circle
UNIT.careers: Illustrative pattern/material-design practices;no real door/site-clearance qualification.
UNIT.focus: Sector/segment boundaries,minor/majorareas,actual safe paper models and bounded design/sweep applications.
UNIT.phenomenon: A fictional decorator removes a circular cap but subtracts a whole wedge and confuses majorsector with majorsegment.
UNIT.drivingQuestion: Which boundaries and measurements justify a circle-part area? KICD: Where do we use area of part of a circle in real life?
UNIT.storylineThread: Boundaries → sector → actualsector → minorsegment → majorcomplement → actualsegment → sweep → capapplication → audit → independent evidence.
UNIT.content: Area of a sector; Area of a segment
UNIT.coreCompetencies:
Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: the learner explores different options of improvising cutouts of sectors of a circle for working out their areas.
Learning to Learn: the learner acquires new knowledge as they discuss with peers how to work out areas of circular objects.
Citizenship; learners appreciate their immediate environment as they gather locally available circular objects
UNIT.values:
Unity: The learner exhibits devotion and honesty by undertaking the task while working with peers to make paper cutouts of sectors of a circle and obtain the measurements.
Peace: the learner displays care and tolerance while discussing with peers and obtaining circular objects, tracing and marking out sectors and segments.
UNIT.pcis: Education for Sustainable Development: the learner uses locally available circular objects to trace and mark out sectors and segments, and work out the areas.
UNIT.subject: Essential Mathematics
UNIT.learningOutcomes:
determine the area of a sector of a circle in different situations,
determine the area of a segment of a circle in different situations,
apply the area of part of a circle in real-life situations,
appreciate the application of area of part of circular objects in real-life situations.

FINAL_EXPLANATION.subjectLabel: AREA OF A PART OF A CIRCLE
FINAL_EXPLANATION.instructions: Lesson10,40minutes:4procedure,12sections1–2,16sections3–4,4silentcheck,4collection. Work independently with CP10only,blankpaper and calculatorπ/degree mode. No teaching cards,peers,hints or media. Show labelled boundaries/formulas/units;retain exactπexpressions and round final nonexact areas to2decimalplaces.

sections.title: 1. Sector boundary and area
sections.prompt: Draw FinalAsector with centre,radii,arc and centralangle labelled. Compute its area. Explain why the arc-length formula would have the wrong units for this question.

sections.title: 2. Minor segment partition
sections.prompt: For FinalBdraw the minor sector,chord and centraltriangle. Compute sector,triangle and minorsegment areas;explain the subtraction and one rounding/measurement limit.

sections.title: 3. Major segment and a useful sweep
sections.prompt: Find FinalBmajorsegment by complement and show the two segment areas sum to the whole circle. Distinguish majorsegment from majorsector. Draw and compute FinalCpaper-door-sweep area,and state a condition/limitation for its use.

sections.title: 4. Application and actual model evidence
sections.prompt: Explain one useful application of sector/segment area and one limit involving boundary choice,fit,waste or actual measurement. Describe one actual individual observation needed before claiming you made/measured a cut-out. Explain why exact fictional data alone do not establish that action.

SUMMARY_TABLE.subStrand: Sub-Strand2.5: Area of a Part of a Circle
SUMMARY_TABLE.drivingQuestion: Which boundaries and measurements justify a circle-part area? KICD: Where do we use area of part of a circle in real life?

lessons.title: Which boundary makes a sector or a segment?
lessons.observed: Distinguish sector/segment and minor/major region boundaries.
lessons.learned: Two radii and an arc bound a sector;chord and arc bound a segment.

lessons.title: How does central angle determine a sector fraction?
lessons.observed: Determine minor/major sector areas from radius and degree angle.
lessons.learned: Sector area is the central-angle fraction ofπr²,with square units.
lessons.explained: Calculate exactπforms and rounded values with correct radius.

lessons.title: Can we make and measure a genuine sector?
lessons.observed: Make/mark and measure a safe actual sector with honest action/precision records.
lessons.learned: A true centre,radius and central angle are necessary for the sector model.
lessons.explained: Trace,locate centre,mark,measure and calculate from actual readings.

lessons.title: Why is a minor segment smaller than its sector?
lessons.observed: Determine a minor segment as matching sector minus central triangle.
lessons.learned: The chord splits off the central isosceles triangle from a minor sector.
lessons.explained: Draw the correct partition and use the included central angle.

lessons.title: How does the major segment differ from the major sector?
lessons.observed: Determine minor/major segment areas and distinguish a major sector.
lessons.learned: The two segments share a chord and sum to the whole circle;major sector has different straight boundaries.
lessons.explained: Use a complement and compare three regions.

lessons.title: What does a measured segment model establish?
lessons.observed: Make/mark and measure an actual segment model using the same centre/radius/angle.
lessons.learned: A segment estimate combines matched geometry and measured quantities with uncertainty.
lessons.explained: Record actual dimensions,partition,calculate and state a precision limit.

lessons.title: What does a door-sweep sector represent?
lessons.observed: Apply sector area to a fictional tabletop sweep and explain its limits.
lessons.learned: A plan-view swept region differs from door-surface area and real safety clearance.
lessons.explained: Draw a model,calculate and justify a useful conditional application.

lessons.title: Which area remains after removing a cap?
lessons.observed: Apply segment subtraction to a decorative model and bound material-use claims.
lessons.learned: Removing a minor cap leaves the major segment,not simply the major sector.
lessons.explained: Partition,calculate and explain a useful design benefit/limit.

lessons.title: Which curved-area claims survive an audit?
lessons.observed: Correct sector/segment,major-region and scale claims with an application reason.
lessons.learned: Boundaries,units and squared radius determine curved-area calculations.
lessons.explained: Audit formulas and justify corrections using labelled regions.
